region.text: the Indian Union as reorganised on 1 November 1956: Madhya Pradesh ('Madhya Bharat, Vindhya Pradesh, and Bhopal State were merged into Madhya Pradesh'), Kerala ('Travancore-Cochin state with the Malabar district'), Rajasthan and the other states

events.note: India holds its states as the States Reorganisation Act made them on 1 November 1956: 'Madhya Bharat, Vindhya Pradesh, and Bhopal State were merged into Madhya Pradesh', and Kerala was 'formed by the merger of Travancore-Cochin state with the Malabar district'. Reviewer: this first sentence is the caption; the window agent's note follows. 1960: the 1 January 1960 anchor leaves 679 cells of the Indian states unowned (539 in Madhya Pradesh, 76 in Kerala, 42 in Rajasthan, a few in eleven others); the republic's 1961 keyframe snap fills 657 of them. The States Reorganisation Act came into effect on 1 November 1956 and made these areas states of the Union, so they are India's from 1 January 1960.

region.text: Bialystok and Podlachia, 'transferred back to Poland' on 20 September 1944, and the Bug-river cells of Lublin province that the Byelorussian shape claims

events.note: Białystok and Podlachia are Polish: 'On 20 September 1944 the city was transferred back to Poland', and under the border agreement of 16 August 1945 'The Belastok Region was divided into Soviet Brest Region, Grodno Region and Polish Białystok Voivodeship'. Reviewer: this first sentence is the caption; the window agent's note follows. 1960: the Podlachian land (93 cells) and 13 cells of Lublin province on the Bug are still drawn as Byelorussian SSR. Bialystok page: the city was 'incorporated into the Byelorussian SSR from 1939 to 1941', 'On 20 September 1944 the city was transferred back to Poland' and became 'capital of the initial Bialystok Voivodeship of the People's Republic of Poland'; Territorial changes of Poland page: 'On August 16, 1945, a border agreement between Poland and the USSR was signed' and the Belastok Region 'was divided into Soviet Brest Region, Grodno Region and Polish Bialystok Voivodeship'.

region.text: the Kingdom of Greece, the whole country with its islands (Crete, the Peloponnese, the Aegean islands)

events.note: Greece, the whole country with its islands, is the kingdom's until the coup of 21 April 1967, when 'the whole of Greece was in the hands of the colonels'. Reviewer: this first sentence is the caption; the window agent's note follows. 1960: 58 cells of Greece (11 on Crete, 11 in the Peloponnese, 6 in Thrace, 6 in Central Greece, 5 in Attica and others) are unowned specks in the Cliopatria shape. The page: the colonels 'seized power' on 21 April 1967 and 'the whole of Greece was in the hands of the colonels', so before that the kingdom held the whole country.

region.text: Okinawa and the Ryukyu Islands under the United States Civil Administration, whose 'ultimate sovereignty remained with Japan'

events.note: Okinawa and the Ryukyu Islands stay under US administration (USCAR, 'effective 15 December 1950') while 'their ultimate sovereignty remained with Japan'. Reviewer: this first sentence is the caption; the window agent's note follows. 1960: Okinawa is still drawn as plain Japanese land. The page: the US military administration began on 22 June 1945, 'USCAR established, effective 15 December 1950', and after the Treaty of San Francisco came into force in April 1952 the islands stayed under US administration while 'their ultimate sovereignty remained with Japan': an occupation without annexation, hatched. (Japan's own ledger opens the occupation in 1945 (ledger/80) but its 1952 end of the home-islands occupation (ledger/112) closes the one occupation the compiler keeps for the pair, so Okinawa is plain Japan from 1952 in the anchor.)

region.text: Okinawa and the Ryukyu Islands under the United States Civil Administration, whose 'ultimate sovereignty remained with Japan'

events.note: Okinawa stays under US administration through 1968: 'control of Okinawa was given back to Japan on 15 May 1972'. Reviewer: this first sentence is the caption; the window agent's note follows. 1968: Japan's ledger closes the US occupation of the Ogasawara group and Iwo Jima in 1968 (ledger/114), and the compiler keys an occupation by the pair of states, so that end also closes the Okinawa hatching. Okinawa stayed under US administration: the page says 'control of Okinawa was given back to Japan on 15 May 1972'. The occupation is opened again here, in December so that it follows the Bonin end.

correction.text: the whole country with its islands: the colonels took over the state of 1963-1967 on 21 April 1967 and 'the whole of Greece was in the hands of the colonels'

keyframe_overrides.why: The Cliopatria shape leaves 60 cells of Greece unowned (Crete 11, Peloponnese 11, Thrace 6, Central Greece 6, Attica 5 and others), so the 1963 snap removes them from the kingdom. The page: 'On 21 April 1967, a group of colonels overthrew a caretaker government' and 'the whole of Greece was in the hands of the colonels'; the kingdom they seized was the whole country.

correction.text: the whole country with its islands under the colonels: 'the whole of Greece was in the hands of the colonels'

keyframe_overrides.why: The Cliopatria shape leaves 62 cells of Greece unowned (Crete 11, Peloponnese 11, South Aegean 7, Thrace 6, Central Greece 6, Attica 5 and others) and the 1967 snap removes them from the junta. The page: the junta 'ruled Greece from 1967 to 1974' and 'the whole of Greece was in the hands of the colonels'.
